commands: DEEPSTREAM_CONTAINER_NAME=aegis-tcn-diag-<ts> bash scripts/deepstream.sh env CONFIG_DIR=/workspace/perception/deepstream/diagnostics CONFIG_PREFIX=trafficcamnet NETWORK_SIZE=544x960 TRACKER_CONFIG=/workspace/perception/deepstream/reference/config_tracker_NvDCF_perf.yml bash /workspace/perception/candidates/rt_detr/diagnostics/run_diagnostic.sh <variant> <out> --with-tracker
findings: Production default nvinfer scaling (1920x1080 -> 960x544) is closest to top-left-aligned nearest sampling (mean abs 0.0042 vs that emulation).
scaling-filter=3 (supersample) is closest to half-pixel bilinear at this ~2x ratio (0.0051); scaling-filter=1 is still nearest-like (0.0145).

Filter choice materially changes output: pre-tracker persons/frame 18.25 (default), 16.84 (bilinear), 15.72 (supersample); unique track IDs 130/118/101; median track length 53/47.5/66 frames; cross-variant same-frame boxes shift 11-20 px median and 2-5 persons appear/disappear.
All variants detect roughly 15-18 persons/frame in a scene where frame 141 visibly contains far more people; TrafficCamNet remains a plumbing smoke model, not a crowd-counting baseline.
decision: No production change. None of the variants can be shown more accurate without labels; this is recorded as a preprocessing sensitivity that any labeled evaluation must fix explicitly in config.
raw_tensor_capture: Not captured in these runs: TrafficCamNet layer names contain '/', so the .npy paths were invalid (recorded in run-summary tensor_errors). Fixed in extract_pretracker.py afterwards; raw tensors were not needed for this analysis.
